
# Appendix B: R5 Spacecraft 2 (R5-S2) and R5 Spacecraft 4 (R5-S4) Flight Results


## Purpose
This file captures basic context and information on the flight performance of the star tracker algorithm onboard R5-S2 and R5-S4.

This is an older version of the software with many limitations on its implementation so it IS NOT recommended to use this 
as a reference for the algorithms performance.  This data set is presented primarily for completeness and as lessons learned.

## Context
R5-S2 and R5-S4 were the first R5 spacecraft to make it to orbit.  They ran the v1.1 version of the COTS Star Tracker software
(approximately commit 8fcd98) with each using a single Ximea MC023 camera with a Fujinon HF35HA lens as the imager.

Both spacecraft were tumbling throughout their missions at a unknown rate, had their telemetry systems configured
to downlink a random sample of the star tracker solutions, and were in LEO.

Publications:
* https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20240009839
* https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20250006508
* https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20250009116
* https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20240016467
* https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20250001957

## Lessons Learned
With so many potential variables impacting the performance of the system, it was determined that additional insight was required
to understand the root cause of the low solve rate.

With the telemetry messages, it was impossible to tell how many star tracker solve attempts were made, leading to future systems
containing both data describing the number of solution attempts and the number of successful solutions.

## Flight Data

### Data Description
* time_met_s is the Mission Elapsed Time in seconds at which point the data was downlinked
* st_time_met_s is the Mission Elapsed Time in seconds at which point the star tracker solution was created
* st_num_imgs is the number of star tracker images currently on disk
* st_img_solve_time_s is the solve time for this image in seconds
* st_img_fname_code is the associated exposure time code for this image with 1 being 50 ms, 2 being 100 ms, and 3 being 250 ms
* qs, qv0, qv1, qv2 are the quaternion constituents
* reconstructed_onboard_unix_time_s is the unix time associated with the time_met_s
* spacecraft is the spacecraft number
